title: What Kind of Lover Are You?

chapters.title: How you fall
chapters.teaser: Fast, slow, sideways or all at once. The way your soul actually falls for someone.

chapters.title: Your flirting style
chapters.teaser: What you think you're doing, what they think you're doing, and the one move that lands.

chapters.title: Your attachment pattern
chapters.teaser: Clingy, cool, steady or somewhere in between. How you hold on when you care.

chapters.title: Jealousy and your trigger
chapters.teaser: The exact thing that sets you off, and what you do instead of saying it.

chapters.title: Yeon's red flag report
chapters.teaser: The love habit you keep repeating. Yeon does not soften this chapter.

chapters.title: What you actually need
chapters.teaser: Not your type. Your match. The kind of person and love that lets you relax.

chapters.how-you-fall: You don't fall, you decide. Somewhere around the third conversation you look at a person and think, yes, this one is worth building something with, and from then on you are all in. Gap is the tall tree, and trees don't wander off to see what else is growing. The catch is that your decision often comes before the other person has made theirs. You can mistake your own certainty for proof that it's mutual. You also fall for potential. You see who someone could become in five years and you love that version a little too early. When it works, it's beautiful: steady, loyal, protective love that makes people feel chosen. When it doesn't, you stay far longer than the evidence allows, because leaving feels like admitting you planted in the wrong field.
chapters.flirting: Your flirting looks a lot like mentoring. You ask about their plans, you give advice nobody requested, you show up with a solution to the problem they mentioned last Tuesday. To you, this is romance. To them, it can feel like a very attractive performance review. You are not a giggler or a hair-twirler. You flirt with competence and reliability, and the people who get it find it irresistible. The people who don't think you're just being nice. Try this: say one thing you like about them that has nothing to do with their potential. Not "you'd be great at this job." Something like "I like how you laugh at your own jokes before the punchline." Small, specific, a little soft. It lands harder than any plan you could make for them.
chapters.attachment: Your pattern sits close to what psychologists would call secure on the surface, with a hidden streak of control underneath. You are steady. You text back. You keep promises. But you also want things to grow in a direction you can see, and when a partner drifts or goes quiet, you don't panic, you start managing. You suggest, you organize, you quietly take over. It feels like care. It can land as pressure. The tree wants to be the thing everyone leans on, and being leaned on feels safer than leaning. The honest question for you is not "do I love well?" You do. It's "can I let someone else hold the plan for a while without checking on it?" That's where your next level of closeness lives.
chapters.jealousy: You don't do loud jealousy. You do principled jealousy. You won't check their phone, because that's beneath you, but you will notice that they replied to someone else's story in four minutes and yours in four hours, and you will file it away. Your trigger is disrespect more than competition. You can handle a partner having attractive friends. What you can't handle is feeling like you were an option rather than the choice. When it hits, you go stiff and formal, which confuses people, because you seem fine and you are absolutely not fine. The fix is boring and it works: say it early, in one plain sentence. "That made me feel like a backup." You're good at direct. Use it on your own feelings, not just everyone else's problems.
chapters.red-flag: Yeon's verdict: you fall in love with projects. You are drawn to people who are a little lost, a little unfinished, because you know exactly how to help them grow. Then you spend the relationship being their coach, their landlord of emotional stability, their five-year plan. They grow, sometimes right out of the relationship, and you're left holding the watering can wondering what happened. The other flag is pride. You'd rather be right than close, and you can hold a position long after you've forgotten why you took it. Neither of these makes you a bad partner. They make you a tired one. Look for someone who is already growing on their own. You don't need to be anyone's sunlight. You get to just be the tree next to them.
chapters.what-you-need: You need a partner with their own roots. Someone who has plans you didn't write, opinions you can't talk them out of, and a life that would keep going if you took a month off from being impressive. You need respect more than you need flattery, and you can tell the difference instantly. You also need someone who notices when you're tired, because you won't say it. The tree doesn't announce that it's thirsty. Practically: you love best with someone who keeps their word, who argues fair, and who lets you lead in some places and takes the lead in others without a power struggle. The love that suits you is less fireworks, more forest. Two tall things growing side by side, close enough to share shade, far enough apart to both get light.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gap, you love like a promise. Steady, loyal, the person everyone wishes they'd dated first.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Also the person who turns a second date into a five-year development plan.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: That's devotion! You see who someone could become.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And then you date who they could become instead of who's actually sitting there.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: The right person already has roots. You don't have to grow them.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Put down the watering can, babe. Nobody asked to be your project.

chapters.how-you-fall: You fall sideways. Eul is the vine and the wildflower, and vines don't charge at things, they wind. One day you're just friends, the next you've memorized their coffee order, their sister's name and the exact playlist that fixes their bad days, and you realize you've been falling for weeks. You attach through closeness and small daily contact. Texting good morning, sharing memes, borrowing their hoodie. It's gentle and it's sneaky, even to you. The beauty of this is that your love feels natural and easy, never forced. The risk is that you can wrap yourself around a person before you've checked whether they're a strong trellis or a wobbly fence post. You adapt to fit them so well that it's hard to tell, later, which parts of you were yours.
chapters.flirting: You are a natural. Flirting is basically your second language, and most of the time you don't even know you're doing it. The tilted head, the "wait, tell me more," the way you remember a detail they mentioned once and bring it up three days later. People feel seen around you, and that's the whole trick. You also flirt in groups beautifully, drawing the quiet one into the conversation so they think you're the warmest person alive. The downside: people sometimes can't tell if you're into them or just being you. If you actually like someone, make it unmistakable once. Ask them to something with just the two of you, and name it. "I'd like to take you to that ramen place. Like a date." Vines are allowed to be direct.
chapters.attachment: Your pattern leans anxious when you care a lot. You read the temperature of a relationship constantly: a shorter reply, a missing emoji, a slight change in how they say your name. You're very good at adjusting to keep the peace, which looks like flexibility but can become disappearing. You'd rather bend than risk a fight, so needs go unsaid and slowly build into a quiet resentment you don't fully show. When you feel secure, though, you are one of the most delightful partners there is: playful, affectionate, socially easy, great at weaving someone into your life and friends. The work for you is noticing the moment you start shrinking to keep someone comfortable. That's your cue to say one true thing, even if your voice shakes a little.
chapters.jealousy: Your jealousy is social. You're not threatened by a stranger, you're threatened by the friend who seems to get them in a way you don't, the coworker with all the inside jokes, the ex they still laugh with. Because connection is your superpower, someone else's connection with your person can feel like a direct competitor. And you're too graceful to make a scene, so you do something worse: you become extra charming, extra helpful, extra easy, trying to win a contest nobody announced. Then you're exhausted. The healthier move is curiosity instead of competition. Ask, lightly, "you two seem close, what's the story?" Most of the time the answer is boring. And when it isn't, at least you'll know, instead of shapeshifting in the dark.
chapters.red-flag: Yeon's verdict: you lose your shape. You become the version of yourself that fits whoever you're dating. With the indie musician you suddenly own vinyl. With the gym person you're up at six. It's charming for a while, and then you look in the mirror and can't remember what you liked before them. Second flag: you avoid conflict so skillfully that problems grow roots under the floorboards. You say "it's fine" with a smile so convincing you almost believe it. Third, smaller one: you keep options open. A little flirting with the backup plan, just in case. You don't mean harm, you just hate the feeling of having nowhere to go. Pick a trellis you actually trust, then stop hedging.
chapters.what-you-need: You need a partner who is genuinely sturdy. Someone calm and consistent, who doesn't swing between hot and cold, so you can stop reading the weather and just grow. You need to be adored out loud, often, in small ways: a text in the afternoon, a hand on your back at a party, being introduced proudly. You also need someone who wants your real opinions, not your agreeable ones, and who keeps asking until they get them. Space matters too, oddly. Vines need to climb, and your friendships, hobbies and little side quests are not a threat to love, they're what keeps you interesting. The best match for you holds steady while you move, and is delighted, not threatened, when you bloom in a direction they didn't predict.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Eul, you love like a vine. Gentle, close, woven into every little part of their day.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And by month three you've adopted their music taste, their friends and their opinions on cilantro.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're just so adaptable! People feel completely seen by you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: People feel seen. You feel invisible. Fun trade.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Say one true thing out loud this week. Your real opinion is part of your charm.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: "It's fine" is not a love language. Stop saying it.

chapters.how-you-fall: You fall fast and in public. Byeong is the sun, and the sun has never once been subtle. When you like someone, everyone knows by Friday, including your group chat, your mum and possibly the barista. You fall for energy: someone who laughs at your jokes, who matches your enthusiasm, who makes ordinary nights feel like an event. The first weeks with you are a highlight reel. Spontaneous plans, big gestures, you making them feel like the most interesting person in any room. The tricky part comes when the shine settles into routine. You love loving, and you can mistake a quiet phase for a dying flame. It usually isn't. Real warmth doesn't need to be at full brightness all the time. Even the sun has evenings.
chapters.flirting: Your flirting is generous and slightly overwhelming, in a fun way. You compliment loudly, you tease, you make the plan, you pay for the snacks, you invite them to the thing with your twelve friends. You flirt like you're hosting. People feel instantly welcome, which is why you're so easy to crush on. The flip side is that your warmth is the same for everyone, so the person you actually like may not realize they're special. They watched you light up the whole table. Here's the move: give them something you don't give the room. Quiet attention. Lower your voice, ask a real question, and stay on their answer for longer than feels natural. Your spotlight is lovely. Your undivided focus is unforgettable.
chapters.attachment: You look secure, and a lot of the time you are. You're optimistic about love, you forgive quickly, you don't hold grudges, you assume the best. Underneath, there's a quieter need: you want to be seen shining. If a partner stops reacting, stops noticing, stops laughing, you don't get anxious exactly, you get bored and a little hurt, and you might go looking for an audience elsewhere. Not cheating, just more attention from friends, more plans, more noise. Your growth edge is staying through the dull middle. Love includes Tuesdays where nothing happens and nobody applauds. If you can feel warm on those days too, without needing a reaction, you become the kind of partner people build whole lives around.
chapters.jealousy: You don't expect to be jealous, so when it hits it surprises you. Your trigger is attention. If your person is lit up by someone else, laughing harder at their jokes, more animated in their conversation, you feel it like a cloud crossing your face. You might not say anything. Instead, you turn the brightness up. Louder stories, bigger plans, more charm aimed in their direction. It works, sometimes, but it's exhausting and a bit transparent. Try naming it with a smile instead: "Okay, I'm a tiny bit jealous of how much you like her jokes." Said lightly, this is disarming and honest. People love you for your openness. Being open about the not-so-sunny feelings is the same skill, just pointed inward.
chapters.red-flag: Yeon's verdict: you make promises at full brightness and keep them at half. "We should go to Jeju together!" "I'll cook you dinner every Sunday!" You mean every word in the moment. Then life happens, and the person who believed you is quietly disappointed. Second flag: you hate heavy talks. When things get serious, you crack a joke, change the subject, or suggest getting food. It feels like keeping things light. To your partner it can feel like you're never fully there for the hard stuff. Third: you need an audience, and a partner can start to feel like one. Love is not a show with a crowd. Make fewer promises, keep more of them, and let someone see you when you're not performing.
chapters.what-you-need: You need appreciation, sincerely and often. Not empty flattery, which you see through, but someone who notices what you do and tells you. "That was so thoughtful." "You made that party." You need a partner with their own glow, too: someone with passions and plans so you don't feel responsible for keeping the whole relationship lit. You do well with people who are calm without being cold, who can be your steady evening when your day has been loud. And you need room to be social. A partner who resents your friends or your plans will dim you fast. The ideal person for you laughs easily, says what they feel, and still loves you on the days you are cloudy and quiet.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Byeong, you love like sunshine. Big, warm, generous. Everyone feels invited.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Exactly. Everyone. Including the person you're not dating. They're confused.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're just naturally warm! Your first dates are legendary.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Your first dates, yes. Your fourth month when it gets quiet and you get restless? Less legendary.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Give your person the attention you don't give the room. That's the real gift.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Fewer promises about Jeju. More actually showing up on Tuesday.

chapters.how-you-fall: You fall slowly and then completely. Jeong is the candle, and candles don't light up a stadium, they light up a face across a small table. You need a real conversation, the kind that goes past midnight and somehow turns into talking about your childhood, before anything in you moves. Once it does, you feel it intensely. You remember everything: the song playing when they first held your hand, the exact phrasing of their text. Your love is intimate, observant and deeply personal. People who are loved by you feel understood in a way they rarely have before. The risk is that you can fall for the inner world you've imagined in someone, filling silences with meaning they didn't intend. Check in with the real person, not just the beautiful version in your head.
chapters.flirting: Your flirting is quiet and devastating. You don't make a show. You listen, you notice, and then you say something so specific that the other person feels like you've read their diary. "You go quiet when people talk about your dad." A little risky, very effective. You flirt through attention and meaning: a song you send at 11pm, a book you think they'd like, a thoughtful question nobody else asked. With people you're not into, you're warm but polite. With someone you like, the warmth gets focused like a flame. The challenge is that it can be so subtle they miss it entirely. Add one obvious signal. Hold eye contact a second longer. Say "I like talking to you." Candles are allowed to flicker on purpose.
chapters.attachment: Your pattern runs warm and anxious when you love deeply. You're emotionally tuned in, which means you also pick up every tiny shift, real or imagined. A cooler goodnight can keep you awake. You may replay conversations and draft replies in your head long before you send anything. You give a lot of care, often more than you ask for, and then quietly feel hurt when it isn't returned in the same careful way. When you feel safe, you are tender, loyal and wonderfully devoted. The work is learning to ask instead of interpret. Your intuition is strong, but it isn't a mind-reading license. "Hey, you seemed off tonight, are we okay?" will save you three days of quiet spiraling.
chapters.jealousy: Your jealousy is private and it burns low and long. You won't cause a scene. You'll go a little quiet, a little formal, and then lie awake replaying the moment they laughed at someone else's story. Your trigger is emotional intimacy. Physical attractiveness in others bothers you less than the idea that someone else gets the deep, real version of your person. If they confide in a friend before you, that stings more than any flirt ever could. Because you're so perceptive, you're sometimes right, and that makes the jealousy feel justified even when it isn't. Try separating facts from stories. Write down what actually happened, then what you're afraid it means. Usually the second list is much longer, and much less true.
chapters.red-flag: Yeon's verdict: you keep a scrapbook of hurts. You forgive out loud, then quietly remember every forgotten anniversary, every careless word, every time you felt second. One day it all comes out at once and your partner is blindsided by a list they didn't know existed. Second flag: the silent test. You'll wait to see if they notice you're upset instead of telling them, and when they don't, it becomes proof they don't really care. Nobody passes a test they don't know they're taking. Third: you can romanticize people who are emotionally unavailable, because their mystery gives your imagination room to work. Light your candle for someone who sits close to it, not someone who stays in the doorway.
chapters.what-you-need: You need emotional presence. A partner who talks about feelings without making it weird, who remembers what matters to you, and who reassures you without needing to be asked every time. You need depth over noise. Big parties and constant plans can tire you out, while a quiet evening cooking together and talking can refill you for a week. You also need someone steady enough that your sensitivity has a safe place to land, and who won't use it against you in a fight. Above all, you need consistency. Not grand gestures, just the same warmth on an ordinary Wednesday as on your birthday. With the right person you burn beautifully for years, a small steady flame that never needs to compete with the sun.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Jeong, you love like candlelight. Close, warm, and so attentive it feels like being read.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And you remember every single thing they did wrong. With dates.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: That's just how deeply you care! You notice everything.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You also give silent tests. They failed the one they didn't know they were taking.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Ask instead of guessing. "Are we okay?" is a beautiful sentence.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Your intuition is strong. It is not a lie detector. Use your words.

chapters.how-you-fall: You fall like a mountain moves: very slowly, and then it's permanent. Mu is the big hill, the boulder, the thing you can lean against without checking. You don't do impulsive crushes. You observe someone for a long time, quietly gathering evidence that they're trustworthy, consistent and worth the effort of letting in. By the time you show interest, you've basically already decided. That means rejection hits harder than you'd ever show. On the bright side, when you choose someone, they feel deeply safe. You become their shelter: the person who drives over in the rain, fixes the shelf, remembers the doctor appointment. The risk is that you're so focused on being solid that your partner might not realize you're also falling, because mountains don't exactly blush.
chapters.flirting: You flirt by being useful, and you may not even call it flirting. Carrying their bags, making sure they got home, showing up with snacks because they mentioned they skipped lunch. It's steady, practical care, and the people who notice it melt. The people who don't might wonder if you're interested at all, because you rarely say the soft thing out loud. Your humour helps a lot here. Dry, understated jokes are your secret weapon, and when you let them out, people get a glimpse of the warm landscape behind the cliff face. Try one small step past comfort: tell them you like them, plainly. You don't need poetry. "I like spending time with you" from a mountain sounds like a whole sonnet.
chapters.attachment: Your pattern looks secure and sometimes leans avoidant. You're reliable and calm, the opposite of dramatic, and you rarely panic about where a relationship stands. But emotional conversations can make you go quiet and still, like a hill waiting out a storm. You'd rather fix a problem than talk about how it feels, and when a partner wants to process, you might reach for solutions or simply shut down until it passes. That's not coldness. It's how you protect a very big, very loyal heart. Your growth edge is staying present in the feelings part. Sit in the conversation without fixing it. Say "that sounds hard" and mean it. You'll be surprised how much closer people feel when the mountain just listens.
chapters.jealousy: You rarely get jealous, and when you do, it looks like nothing. That's the problem. You don't sulk or accuse. You just become a little more distant, a little more silent, and quietly start reconsidering how much you trust this person. Your trigger is inconsistency. If someone says one thing and does another, flirts openly when they promised they wouldn't, or hides something small, your entire internal foundation shifts. You don't care much about rivals. You care about reliability. Because you don't express it, the other person might not realize there's anything wrong until you've already half withdrawn. Say it while it's still small. "I noticed this and it bothered me." Mountains erode slowly. It's better to repair one crack than rebuild the whole slope.
chapters.red-flag: Yeon's verdict: you're stubborn to the point of geology. Once you've decided how something should go, you stop listening, and your partner feels like they're arguing with a wall. A very kind, very supportive wall, but a wall. Second flag: you mistake stability for romance. You can stay comfortable in a relationship that stopped growing years ago because it's familiar and safe. "Nothing's wrong" is not the same as "this is good." Third: you shut down instead of fighting. The silent treatment isn't punishment for you, it's processing, but to your partner it feels like being frozen out. You're allowed to need time. Just say "I need an hour, then let's talk" instead of disappearing into rock.
chapters.what-you-need: You need trust, and you need it earned. A partner who is consistent, keeps small promises, and doesn't play games, because you have zero patience for mind tricks. You need someone who appreciates quiet loyalty and doesn't need constant performance of affection to feel loved. Gentle encouragement helps you too: someone who invites you to try new things without pushing, who brings a little colour and spontaneity to your steady life. And you need someone who understands that your love shows up as action. When you cook for them or sort out their car, that's a declaration. The best person for you feels like a clear day on a mountain. Calm, open, and worth staying for.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Mu, you love like a mountain. Solid, protective, the safest place anyone's ever stood.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Also about as emotionally chatty as a mountain.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Your love is in actions! You drive over in the rain.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And when they want to talk about feelings, you suggest fixing the shelf.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Try saying "I like you" out loud. From you it sounds like poetry.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Comfortable is not the same as happy. Check which one you're in.

chapters.how-you-fall: You fall by tending. Gi is the garden soil, the field that feeds everything planted in it. You notice what someone needs before they do: the snack, the charger, the reassurance after a bad day at work. Caring for them is how you realize you like them, often after you've already been doing it for weeks. Your love is warm, attentive and incredibly practical. Partners feel looked after in a way that's rare. The danger is that you can confuse being needed with being loved. You might fall for people who need a lot of tending, because being useful feels safe, and slowly end up doing the emotional housework for two. Ask yourself early: if I stopped helping, would they still want me here? With the right person, the answer is an obvious yes.
chapters.flirting: You flirt like a really good host. You check if they're comfortable, you remember they don't like spicy food, you send them the article about the thing they mentioned. People feel calm and cared for around you, and that quiet warmth is extremely attractive. You're also funnier than people expect, with an earthy, self-deprecating humour that sneaks up on them. What you don't do is make the first obvious move. You'd rather create the perfect conditions and wait for them to step in, like planting seeds and hoping for rain. Sometimes it works. Sometimes the other person thinks you're just nice to everyone. Try being the rain once. Send the text that says "I'd like to see you again, just us." The garden will forgive you for being bold.
chapters.attachment: Your pattern leans anxious, mostly in your head. You overthink. A message left on read can turn into a full internal investigation: did I say too much, was I boring, are they losing interest? You often worry quietly and keep giving, hoping care will secure the bond. When things are good, you're a gentle, loyal and deeply reassuring partner, the person who makes home feel like home. The tricky part is that you rarely ask for reassurance directly, so you end up both anxious and helpful at the same time, which is tiring. The growth step for you is asking for what you give. You offer comfort constantly. Let yourself say, "I'm feeling a bit insecure, can you remind me we're good?" It's not needy. It's fair.
chapters.jealousy: Your jealousy comes dressed as worry. You don't think "I'm jealous," you think "I'm not enough." When your person spends time with someone fun, attractive or impressive, you quietly compare and find yourself lacking. Then you over-function: more care, more favours, more effort to be indispensable. Your trigger is feeling replaceable. Because you give so much, the idea that someone else could step in and be liked more easily feels unfair, and it is a little unfair, in your head. The answer isn't to give more. It's to let your partner show you you're chosen. Ask a direct question instead of competing in silence. And notice: people don't stay with you because you're useful. They stay because you make life feel softer.
chapters.red-flag: Yeon's verdict: you mother your partners. You manage their laundry, their schedule, their emotional state and their relationship with their own mum, and then wonder why the romance feels like childcare. Second flag: martyr mode. You quietly do everything and quietly keep score, then feel unappreciated when nobody notices the score exists. Third: overthinking. You can create an entire breakup in your head out of one slightly short reply and be sad about it before anything actually happens. None of this comes from a bad place. It comes from caring too much and asking too little. Stop fertilizing people who don't plant anything back. You deserve someone who brings you snacks, too.
chapters.what-you-need: You need someone who gives back without being asked. A partner who notices your effort and returns it, who makes you tea when you're the one who's tired, who plans the date for once. You need warmth and steadiness more than excitement. Grand gestures are nice, but what really reassures you is consistency: the same goodnight text, the same easy affection, the same calm answer when you ask if everything is okay. You also need encouragement to take up space. You're used to supporting other people's plans, so someone who asks "and what do you want?" is quietly life-changing for you. The best match makes you feel like the garden and the person sitting in it, not just the ground everyone walks on.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gi, you love like a garden. Patient, nurturing, everyone around you just grows.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You also love like an unpaid personal assistant. With overtime.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're so caring! People feel completely at home with you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And you're overthinking that two-word reply right now. I can tell.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Ask for the care you give. You're allowed to be looked after too.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Being needed is not the same as being loved. Know the difference.

chapters.how-you-fall: You fall like a sword is drawn: decisively and with commitment. Gyeong is raw metal, the axe, the blade that has to be forged. You don't do vague. You know pretty quickly if you're interested, and once you are, you pursue with clarity. No games, no hints, just "I like you, let's go to dinner." This directness is refreshing and a little intimidating. You fall for strength, honesty and people who don't fold the first time you push back. Respect comes first. Without it, attraction dies fast. When you love, you love loyally and protectively, the kind of partner who would fight the world for their person. The catch is that you can treat love a bit like a mission, and a mission sometimes forgets to stop and enjoy the view.
chapters.flirting: You flirt by challenging. You tease, debate, poke holes in their opinions and see if they push back. If they do, you're delighted. If they shrink, you lose interest. It's an unusual style, and with the right person it creates incredible sparks. With the wrong one it can feel like being cross-examined. You're also extremely honest, so compliments from you are rare and therefore powerful. When you say "you look good," people believe it. Your growth area is softness. Let yourself be playful without winning, or admit you're nervous. "I'm actually a bit nervous right now" from someone as confident as you is incredibly disarming. The blade is impressive. The hand that holds it gently is what people fall for.
chapters.attachment: Your pattern often looks avoidant, though it comes from independence, not fear. You're self-sufficient and value your freedom, so you don't like being needed in a clingy way and can feel suffocated if a partner wants constant check-ins. You also protect yourself by being strong. Vulnerability can feel like weakness, so you might keep softer feelings locked up, even from people you love. Underneath that armour, you're intensely loyal and deeply sentimental. You'd remember a promise for a decade. The work for you is letting someone see you uncertain, hurt or soft, and staying in the room while they see it. Strength isn't never needing anyone. Strength is choosing to need someone and trusting them with it.
chapters.jealousy: When you're jealous, you get sharp, fast. Your trigger is disloyalty or disrespect. If someone flirts with your partner, or your partner seems to enjoy it a little too much, you feel it as a breach of a code. Your first instinct might be to confront the situation directly, or to cut the person off, possibly both before breakfast. The intensity can scare people, even when you're technically right. The better move is pausing before the swing. Ask yourself what actually happened, then talk to your partner, not the rival. "That bothered me, can we talk about where the line is?" You're great at boundaries. Just make sure you set them in a conversation, not in a showdown.
chapters.red-flag: Yeon's verdict: you love like a drill sergeant. You have standards, rules, and opinions on how your partner should handle their job, their friends and their sock drawer. You call it honesty. They sometimes call it criticism. Second flag: your pride. Apologizing feels like losing, so you'd rather go silent for two days than say "I was wrong." Third: all-or-nothing endings. When someone disappoints you badly enough, you can cut them out instantly and completely, no conversation, no closure. It feels clean. It also means you never find out whether it could have been fixed. You're a protector, and that's beautiful. Just remember your partner is not a recruit. They're the person you chose.
chapters.what-you-need: You need someone strong enough to stand next to you without being cut. A partner with their own spine, their own opinions and enough confidence to tell you no. You need respect in both directions, and honesty even when it's uncomfortable. You also need warmth, quietly. Someone who softens your edges without trying to blunt you, who brings fun and lightness into your very serious, very competent life. You do best with partners who give you independence and don't take your need for space personally. And you need someone patient enough to wait for your heart to open, because when it does, it's huge. The right person makes you feel like metal in a warm fire: shaped, not melted.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gyeong, you love like a sword. Loyal, protective, you'd fight the whole world for your person.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You'd also fight your person. About how they load the dishwasher.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're just honest! Your compliments actually mean something.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Rare compliments, frequent corrections. Not a great ratio, babe.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Show them the soft side. Saying "I'm nervous" makes you more magnetic, not less.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: "I was wrong" won't kill you. Try it once and see.

chapters.how-you-fall: You fall for the details. Sin is the jewel, the polished silver ring, metal that has already been refined into something beautiful. You notice how someone dresses, how they speak to waiters, whether they text in full sentences. Taste matters to you more than you'd admit. When someone passes your many quiet tests, you fall gracefully and with real tenderness. You make love feel elegant and special, like being invited into a beautiful room. Underneath the polish, though, you're sensitive. A careless comment can stay with you for weeks, and you might pull back before you're hurt, just in case. You also fall for an idea of perfection sometimes, and real people, with their messy kitchens and odd habits, can never quite match it. Let them be imperfect. So are you.
chapters.flirting: Your flirting is refined and slightly mysterious. A well-timed compliment, a glance, a perfectly chosen gift that shows you noticed exactly what they like. You're elegant without trying, and people often feel slightly nervous around you because you seem so put together. You also flirt through banter: witty, a little cutting, always clever. The issue is that you can be so polished that people can't tell if you like them or if this is simply your default charm. And you hate rejection so much that you rarely risk being clear. Try letting one crack show. A slightly embarrassing story, a real laugh, a direct "I've been hoping you'd text." The jewel shines brighter when it catches light, and light gets in through the cracks.
chapters.attachment: Your pattern leans anxious under a cool surface. You present calm and composed, but inside you're constantly reading for signs of rejection or disapproval. Criticism stings you deeply, even gentle, well-meant criticism, and you might replay a small comment for days. Because you hate being seen as needy, you rarely ask for reassurance. Instead you withdraw, go a little icy, and wait for the other person to come and find you. If they don't, you take it as confirmation. When you feel secure, you're devoted, thoughtful and wonderfully romantic, with an eye for beauty that makes everyday moments feel special. The work is telling your partner when something hurt, gently and quickly, before it hardens into distance.
chapters.jealousy: Your jealousy is about comparison. You notice the person who seems more beautiful, more successful, more effortlessly cool, and you quietly measure yourself against them. You won't admit it, of course. You'd rather die than appear insecure. So you go cool and slightly sarcastic, and your partner feels a chill without understanding why. Your trigger is being outshone or taken for granted. You put a lot of care into how you love, and you need it noticed. The healthier version is honesty with a light touch. "I felt a bit invisible tonight" is small, true and much more effective than a frosty silence. People who love you want to reassure you. Give them the chance, instead of making them guess why the temperature dropped.
chapters.red-flag: Yeon's verdict: you're a perfectionist in love, and nobody passes inspection. You notice their posture in photos, their grammar in texts, the way they chew, and you file every flaw away until the list is longer than the reasons you liked them. Second flag: you punish with coldness. When hurt, you go elegant and icy, perfectly polite and completely unreachable, which is somehow worse than shouting. Third: your pride can make you leave first just so you don't get left. You'd rather end something beautiful than risk being disappointed by it. You deserve a love that feels precious. Precious doesn't mean flawless. Sometimes the best jewellery has a little wear on it from being loved.
chapters.what-you-need: You need gentleness and appreciation. A partner who notices the effort you put into everything and says so, who gives feedback kindly and never mocks your sensitivity. You need someone with taste, or at least curiosity, who enjoys the beautiful things you love: the good café, the thoughtful gift, the evening that feels curated. You also need a lot of reassurance delivered without drama, and someone who stays warm when you go cool. And you need space to be private. You open slowly, and pressure makes you close faster. The best person for you treats you like something precious without putting you on a shelf. Admired, protected, and still allowed to be human.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, you love like a jewel. Elegant, thoughtful, everything you touch feels special.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And you judged their font choice in the group chat. Don't lie.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You have beautiful taste! People feel honoured to be chosen by you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: When you're hurt, you go so polite it's terrifying. Ice queen behaviour.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Tell them gently when something stings. They want to make it right.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Nobody passes inspection. Stop inspecting. Start enjoying.

chapters.how-you-fall: You fall like a wave: big, sudden and with a pull that surprises everyone, including you. Im is the ocean, the great river, water that moves and refuses to stay still. You're drawn to people who make life feel bigger, the ones who talk about moving to Lisbon on a whim or who can keep up with your curiosity at 2am. You fall through adventure and ideas. A great conversation is your favourite kind of date. The first phase with you is thrilling: spontaneous trips, deep talks, the feeling of being swept up. The trouble comes when the tide turns into routine. You love freedom, and any whiff of being contained can make you drift. That's not because you don't care. It's because oceans need room. Find someone who swims, not someone who builds a pool.
chapters.flirting: Your flirting is effortless and a little hypnotic. You're curious, you ask interesting questions, and you make people feel like the most fascinating person you've met all month. You're great at playful mystery: answering a question with a question, leaving at the right moment, texting something intriguing then going quiet. It's magnetic, and you know it. The risk is that people can't tell if you're serious or just enjoying the current. Also, you might flirt with three people at once, not out of malice but because you genuinely find everyone interesting. If you like someone for real, slow the wave down. Make a plan and keep it. Show up on time. For a person who's used to you drifting, reliability is the most romantic thing you can offer.
chapters.attachment: Your pattern often looks avoidant, driven by freedom more than fear. You love deeply, but you hate feeling trapped, so you might pull back when things get too close too fast, then return when you've had room to breathe. It can confuse partners who need consistency. You also intellectualize feelings. You'll analyze your relationship like a fascinating case study instead of just feeling it. When you trust someone, though, you're generous, open-minded and wonderfully accepting. You rarely judge, and partners feel free around you. The work is telling people your rhythm before it confuses them. "I need some space sometimes, it's not about you" said early saves everyone a lot of worry. The ocean is less scary when people know about the tides.
chapters.jealousy: You rarely get jealous in the usual way. You're too busy with your own life to monitor someone else's. When it does hit, it's often about freedom: if your partner seems to have a more exciting life without you, or someone else gets to share an adventure you wanted, you feel a sudden, surprising pang. Your trigger is being left behind or left out. You might react by becoming more distant, as if to prove you don't care, or by planning something big to reclaim the spotlight. Neither helps much. The honest move is admitting it, which is weirdly hard for you. "I wish I'd been there" is a vulnerable, simple sentence. Water can be deep without being cold.
chapters.red-flag: Yeon's verdict: you disappear. Not dramatically, just a little more quiet every week, until your partner is texting into the void. You call it needing space. They call it being ghosted by someone who still lives with them. Second flag: commitment allergy. You love the start of things and get restless the moment it starts to feel like forever. Third: you keep a few currents running. Old flames, interesting strangers, the one who "just gets you." You don't think of it as betrayal, because nothing happened. But keeping doors half open is its own kind of not choosing. Freedom is part of who you are, and it's beautiful. Just make sure your freedom isn't costing someone else their peace.
chapters.what-you-need: You need freedom and a partner who isn't threatened by it. Someone with their own big life, their own passions and plans, who's happy to have adventures together and also happy when you go off to have one alone. You need intellectual connection. A person who reads, wonders, argues and asks "what if." Boredom is your greatest relationship risk, so someone who keeps surprising you is gold. You also need, though you'd rarely say it, a steady harbour: someone calm and reliable you can always return to. The best match for you doesn't try to hold the water still. They're the shore it keeps coming back to, again and again, by choice.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Im, you love like the ocean. Big, adventurous, people feel swept away by you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And then the tide goes out and they're standing alone on the beach.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You just need freedom! You never try to change anyone.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You also keep three old flames on low heat. Just in case.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Tell them your rhythm early. Tides are less scary when people know they're coming.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Needing space is fine. Vanishing for a week is not "space."

chapters.how-you-fall: You fall like mist settles: quietly, gradually, and then everything is soft and changed. Gye is the rain, the dew, the gentle water that soaks into everything. You don't fall for loud people. You fall for someone who feels like a secret, someone whose inner world seems as layered as yours. Often you fall in your imagination first, writing whole stories about a person before you've had a proper conversation. Your love is romantic, intuitive and deeply emotional. You sense what your partner feels before they say it. The danger is that your imagination can be more beautiful than reality, and you might stay loyal to a dream long after the actual person stopped showing up for it. Love the real one, too, not just the one in your head.
chapters.flirting: Your flirting is subtle, dreamy and a bit hard to catch. A shy smile, a song recommendation that says everything you won't, a meaningful look across the room. You're excellent at making people feel deeply understood, because you really do pick up on their moods. You often flirt through creativity: a drawing, a playlist, a poem in the notes app you might never send. The trouble is that many people miss your signals completely, and you'd rather vanish than risk being too obvious. Here's a gentle challenge. Send the thing. The playlist, the text, the "I've been thinking about you." Rain doesn't apologize for falling. And the people worth having are usually waiting for exactly that kind of quiet courage.
chapters.attachment: Your pattern can lean anxious, with a fearful streak. You crave closeness, but you also fear being truly seen and then left, so you might pull someone in and then go mysteriously quiet. Your moods shift like weather, and partners can find you hard to read even when you're simply feeling a lot. You sense every change in them, too, and can absorb their stress as if it were yours. When you feel safe, you're tender, devoted and astonishingly emotionally attuned, the kind of partner who knows exactly what you need on a bad day. The work for you is putting feelings into words and trusting someone with them. Your sensitivity isn't too much. It just needs the right person, and a little more saying instead of hinting.
chapters.jealousy: Your jealousy is quiet and imaginative. You don't need evidence. Your mind can build an entire storyline out of a like on a photo or a vague "I'll be out with friends." Your trigger is feeling emotionally replaced, that someone else might understand your person more deeply than you. You rarely confront it. Instead you retreat, become distant and dreamy, and wait for your partner to notice. If they don't, the story in your head gets darker. Here's the thing: your intuition is real, but your anxiety borrows its voice. Before acting, ask yourself which one is speaking. Then say the feeling simply. "I got a bit in my head tonight." Rain is gentle. Your honesty can be gentle, too.
chapters.red-flag: Yeon's verdict: you fall for fictional characters and real people who act like fictional characters. Emotionally unavailable, mysterious, "complicated," always just out of reach. The more unavailable, the more poetic it feels. Second flag: you hint instead of ask. You expect partners to read your moods like you read theirs, and when they can't, you feel unloved. That's a test nobody can pass. Third: escaping. When things get hard, you drift into your phone, your daydreams, your playlists, and leave the real conversation hanging. None of this makes you less lovable. It makes you a little lost in the fog. Pick someone who stays when the sky is clear, not just someone who makes the rain feel romantic.
chapters.what-you-need: You need emotional safety, more than anything. A partner who is gentle, patient and consistently kind, so your sensitive nature can finally relax instead of scanning for danger. You need someone who asks about your inner world and is genuinely interested in the answers, your dreams, your weird thoughts, the song that made you cry. You also need grounding. A practical, steady person can help you feel secure without dimming your imagination. And you need words, often. Reassurance said out loud does more for you than any grand gesture. The best person for you is like a calm lake for the rain to fall into. Quiet, deep, and always there when you land.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Gye, you love like soft rain. Gentle, romantic, you feel everything they feel.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You also wrote a whole love story about someone you've spoken to twice.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You're just so intuitive! Your playlists are love letters.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Love letters you never send. Then you're sad they didn't reply.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Send the playlist. Quiet courage is your most beautiful kind.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: "Complicated" is not a personality. Stop dating mysteries. Date someone who texts back.

by_element_balance.too_much_wood: Too much Wood in your chart turns love into a growth plan. You want things to move forward, define the relationship, make progress, and slow phases make you restless. You can also be stubborn in arguments, holding your position like a tree in wind. In love this looks like big intentions and a little impatience. Balance it with Metal energy: clear agreements, pruning what isn't working, and accepting that some things are already finished growing. Not every relationship needs to become a forest. Some are perfect as a single, steady tree.
by_element_balance.missing_wood: Missing Wood means beginnings are your hard part. You might wait for the other person to make the first move, define things, or suggest the next step, and you can stay in a comfortable but stuck situation for too long. Your love is real, it just doesn't push. Balance it by practising small starts: suggest the date, send the first text, say what you hope for out loud. Green things help as reminders, a plant by your bed, a green phone case. Love grows when someone plants it. Sometimes that someone is you.
by_element_balance.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your love bright, fast and a little combustible. You fall hard, flirt boldly and feel everything at full volume. The highs are glorious. The lows, when attention drops, feel like the lights went out. You can also lose interest once the excitement settles. Balance it with Water energy: slowing down, letting quiet evenings count, and sitting with feelings before reacting. Ask yourself if you love the person or the thrill. The best flame for you burns steady, not just bright.
by_element_balance.missing_fire: Missing Fire means passion and visibility don't come easily in love. You might care deeply but struggle to show it, hold back affection until you're sure, or feel awkward with romantic gestures. People can mistake your reserve for disinterest. Balance it by letting warmth out in small, brave doses: a compliment, a hug that lasts a second longer, a little playfulness. Warm colours and sunlight help you feel more expressive. You don't need fireworks. You just need people to see that the light is on.
by_element_balance.too_much_earth: Too much Earth makes you a steady, devoted partner who can get a little stuck. You value security, routine and loyalty, and you might stay in familiar patterns even when they've stopped making you happy. Change feels risky. You may also over-care, taking on your partner's problems as your own. Balance it with Wood energy: try something new together, plan an adventure, let the relationship grow in surprising directions. Safe is wonderful. Safe and alive is even better.
by_element_balance.missing_earth: Missing Earth means love can feel unsteady. You might worry about where things stand, struggle to settle into commitment, or jump between highs and lows. You can also find it hard to trust that someone will stay. Balance it by building small, reliable rituals: a weekly date, a regular call, a shared routine. Choose partners who are consistent rather than exciting. Earth tones and home-cooked meals help you feel grounded. Stability isn't boring. For you, it's what lets love feel safe enough to enjoy.
by_element_balance.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives you strong standards and very clear boundaries in love. You know what you want and what you won't tolerate, which is healthy, until it becomes rigid. You can be critical, quick to judge, or end things abruptly when disappointed. Balance it with Fire energy: warmth, forgiveness, play. Let small mistakes be small. Say the kind thing before the honest thing. Strong boundaries keep you safe. Soft edges let people actually come close enough to love you.
by_element_balance.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are your hard part in love. You might say yes when you mean no, stay too long, or let people treat you less well than you deserve because you don't want conflict. Your heart is open, sometimes too open. Balance it by practising clear, simple limits: "I'm not okay with that," without a long explanation. Decluttering and white or silver accents can help you feel sharper. Boundaries aren't walls. They're the frame that makes the picture of your love clear.
by_element_balance.too_much_water: Too much Water makes your love deep, intuitive and sometimes overwhelming. You feel everything, read every mood and can get lost in emotional currents or imagined stories. You may also avoid commitment, drifting rather than choosing. Balance it with Earth energy: grounding conversations, practical plans, partners who are steady and clear. Write down what actually happened before reacting to what you feel happened. Your depth is beautiful. It just needs a shore so you don't get swept away.
by_element_balance.missing_water: Missing Water means emotional depth and rest don't come easily in love. You might stay busy, keep conversations practical, or struggle to sit with vulnerable feelings, yours or your partner's. Love can feel like a to-do list. Balance it with slow, quiet moments: late talks, journaling, listening without fixing. Navy and black, water by your bed, and slow evenings help you soften. You don't need to drown in feelings. Just let yourself wade in a little deeper.
